verdict.rationale: Independent results show the 285K is faster than the 14900K and roughly on par with the 9950X in at least one score. However, the 9950X comes out ahead in raw performance, and the Windows launch needed fixes for single-threaded performance consistency, so 'leading' single-thread performance is not demonstrated; Intel's own evidence offers only the 5.70 GHz peak clock the story discounts. Missing for 10: an independent single-thread benchmark showing category leadership, evidence of consistent snappy interactive responsiveness, and a first-party single-thread performance claim beyond peak GHz.

support.subject: As a power-user, everyday interactive work feels instant — leading single-thread performance shown in independent benchmarks, not just a peak-GHz number on a slide

citations.quote: Compared to its predecessor, 14900K, it ends up both faster (barring some outliers) and significantly more power efficient.
